title: Multiplication of 4-Digit by 3-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiplication Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiply at least whole 4-digit by 3-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 multiplication worksheets: multiplying by multiples of 10, 3-digit by 2-digit and 4-digit by 3-digit numbers and word problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Units, tens, hundreds, then add the partial products.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Break the second number into hundreds, tens and units: 2 345 × 216 = 2 345 × 200 + 2 345 × 10 + 2 345 × 6.
  • In columns, multiply by the units, then by the tens (write one 0), then by the hundreds (write two 0s).
  • Add the partial products.
  • Estimate first: 2 345 × 216 is about 2 000 × 200 = 400 000.

Examples

Example

2 345 × 216

2 345 × 200 = 469 000

2 345 × 16 = 37 520

Answer: 506 520

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing zerosMultiplying by hundreds needs two 0s.
Forgetting to carryAdd the carried digit.
Adding wronglyLine up the partial products.

items.q: What is 715 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves every digit two places to the left: 715 ones become 715 hundreds. Write two zeros: 715 × 100 = 71 500.

items.q: The school kitchen serves 296 lunches each week. How many lunches does it serve in 38 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 38 weeks × 296 lunches, so multiply 296 × 38. Row 1: 296 × 8 = 2 368. Row 2: 296 × 30 = 8 880 (write the place-holder 0, then 296 × 3 = 888). Add: 2 368 + 8 880 = 11 248.

items.q: Dumisani says 2 345 × 28 = 23 450. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 2 345 rounds to 2 000 and 28 rounds to 30. 2 000 × 30 = 60 000. 23 450 is far from 60 000, so the answer cannot be right. The correct answer is 65 660; Dumisani forgot the place-holder 0 in the second row.

items.q: A delivery driver drives 1 566 km each week. How far does she drive in 23 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 weeks × 1 566 km, so multiply 1 566 × 23. Row 1: 1 566 × 3 = 4 698. Row 2: 1 566 × 20 = 31 320 (write the place-holder 0, then 1 566 × 2 = 3 132). Add: 4 698 + 31 320 = 36 018.

items.q: A farm packs 144 eggs in each crate. It sends 26 crates on Monday and 38 crates on Tuesday. How many eggs does it send altogether?
Vusi swims 64 lengths of a 25 m pool over a term. How far does he swim?
items.e: Equal groups: 64 lengths × 25 m, so multiply 64 × 25. Row 1: 64 × 5 = 320. Row 2: 64 × 20 = 1 280 (write the place-holder 0, then 64 × 2 = 128). Add: 320 + 1 280 = 1 600.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 26 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 26 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 26. Row 1: 144 × 6 = 864. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2 880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 864 + 2 880 = 3 744.

items.q: Priya says 4 127 × 63 = 12 381. Estimate to check. Is her answer sensible?
items.e: 4 127 rounds to 4 000 and 63 rounds to 60. 4 000 × 60 = 240 000. 12 381 is far from 240 000, so the answer cannot be right. The correct answer is 260 001; Priya only multiplied by the ones digit.

items.q: A garden centre has 36 trays of plants. Each tray holds 45 plants. How many plants is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 36 trays × 45 plants, so multiply 45 × 36. Row 1: 45 × 6 = 270. Row 2: 45 × 30 = 1 350 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 3 = 135). Add: 270 + 1 350 = 1 620.

items.q: A coach has 53 seats. It is full on every one of its 24 trips to the seaside this summer. How many passengers is that altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 trips × 53 passengers, so multiply 53 × 24. Row 1: 53 × 4 = 212. Row 2: 53 × 20 = 1 060 (write the place-holder 0, then 53 × 2 = 106). Add: 212 + 1 060 = 1 272.

items.q: Mpho says 689 × 52 = 35 828. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 689 rounds to 700 and 52 rounds to 50. 700 × 50 = 35 000. 35 828 is close to 35 000, so the answer is sensible. (It is also exactly right.)
